subject: Metrics grounding memo — preparing QBR (latency, cost, uptime, usage)
messages:
From: Paul Davis <paul.davis@acme-analytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Monthly metrics ahead of QBR?

Hi Mina,

We're pulling together our QBR pack for the 6th and trying to ground out a few platform metrics so leadership has confidence in recommendation areas. Can you confirm the following for the past 30 days (Aug 29 — Sep 28):
- p50/p95/p99 latency for text generation (hosted API) and for Dedicated (avg across customer pools)
- Cost per 1k tokens pre/ post the recent batching rule change (Aug 10)
- Uptime by region (us-west/us-east/eu) and any incidents impacting SLA windows
- Active app usage: daily active apps and top 5 customers by API calls (anonymized is fine)

We have a short slot in the QBR to call out production risks and ops asks. If you can get a dashboard export or short memo by EOD Friday that would be great.

Appreciate it — Paul
Paul Davis
Director, Platform Analytics
Acme Analytics

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Monthly metrics ahead of QBR?  [internal note]

Team — forwarding Paul's request. External asked for 30-day snapshot and a short memo for the QBR (slot on Oct 6). I'm dropping external from the loop for internal coordination; we'll consolidate a single memo + dashboard export and send to Paul by Friday EOD PT.

Quick proposed division of labor:
- Markus: latency breakdown (hosted vs dedicated), p50/p95/p99 and notes on the Aug 10 batching change impact. Include a brief statement on whether the change materially affected p99 for long-seq workloads.
- Laura: cost deltas and cost-by-cluster CSV; also annotate any recent pricing-config changes for enterprise accounts.
- Tessa: uptime by region, incidents since Jul 1 that could affect SLAs, and the active-apps anonymized top-5 list.
- I'll stitch into a 2-pager memo, attach the CSV and heatmap, and do the external write-back.

Thresholds / asks for write-back memo: be explicit when a metric is an estimate vs. exact (e.g., anonymized top-5). If you include charts, prefer the single-image summary + 1–2 bullet commentary.

Attachments: I'm pulling the current draft dashboards (see Drive link below).

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Monthly metrics ahead of QBR?  [latency + notes]

Mina / team — I've pulled the latency artifacts and an initial heatmap. Highlights: 
- Hosted API (aggregate): p50=42ms, p95=180ms, p99=420ms (for August 29–Sep 28).
- Dedicated pools (weighted avg across committed clusters): p50=36ms, p95=150ms, p99=380ms. Dedicated shows tighter tail due to reserved capacity; outliers are correlated with long-sequence evaluation jobs.
- Aug 10 batching change: average per-token CPU decreased ~6% on medium seqs; however we saw a transient p99 bump (~+18%) for sequences >2048 tokens during the first 72 hours due to scheduling churn. That was resolved with a scheduler tweak on Aug 13.

Notes for memo: call out the transient p99 bump and that it was mitigated — suggests that recent batching helped cost but required a short stabilization window.

Attachments: p99-latency-heatmap-aug2026.png (attached), per-endpoint-latency-table.csv (on Drive).

-Markus
Markus Klein
Sr. Infrastructure Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Paul Davis <paul.davis@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Monthly metrics ahead of QBR?

Paul — thanks for the ask and the pointer to the QBR slot. Attached is a short memo + dashboard exports that address your bullets. High-level callouts below and attachments referenced inline.

Key findings (30-day window: 2026-08-29 to 2026-09-28):
- Latency (hosted API): p50=42ms / p95=180ms / p99=420ms. Dedicated pools: p50=36ms / p95=150ms / p99=380ms. See p99-latency-heatmap-aug2026.png.
- Cost: cost-per-1k-tokens decreased ~4.8% overall after Aug 10 batching rule change; the delta is larger (~7%) for mid-length workloads (seq 512–2048) that gain from batching. CSV attached: cost-by-cluster-aug2026.csv.
- Uptime: All regions met our 99.95% monthly availability target. There were two minor incidents (2026-09-04 maintenance-induced routing blip; 2026-09-18 brief DB failover) — both contained and outside the SLA impact window. Full incident notes in the memo.
- Usage: active apps (anonymized) held steady month-over-month; top-5 customers accounted for 48% of API calls (anonymized list included).

Ops asks for QBR call:
1) Endorse the scheduling tweak made on Aug 13 as the recommended approach for similar rollout windows — it reduced p99 tails without reversing cost gains.
2) Approve a short burst-capacity test next week (2 hours) in us-east to validate tail behavior under peak-eval workloads; we'll publish results within 48 hours.
3) Request leadership alignment on publishing a 1-line footnote in the QBR about the Aug 10 change and transient p99 bump — transparency to customers reduces churn risk.

Attachments: monthly-kpi-pack-2026-08.pdf; p99-latency-heatmap-aug2026.png; cost-by-cluster-aug2026.csv

If you'd like a 10-minute pre-QBR readout, happy to join — suggest Oct 4 at 9:00am PT.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
